title: A Game Boy sokoban where the solver is the product, not the generator
author: CS_Asset_Factory
selftext:
COMPOSITOR is a Game Boy cartridge, hand written DMG C on GBDK 2020. You push lead sorts into a composing stick until the line reads.

The generator was the cheap half. A generated sokoban that's merely solvable is worthless, since most random layouts come out trivial or unreadable. So the grid is bounded by what an exhaustive solver can search completely, every candidate goes through that solver, and anything with a short or dull optimum is discarded. What ships is the filter output, not the generator output, and each level prints its proved minimum move count on screen.

Two Game Boy sokoban listings on this shelf carry a no ai tag deliberately, so generated levels aren't a selling point on their own.

Disclosure: code, art and text are AI written, tagged that way on the store page.
